notes.subject: plate
notes.text: Short white plates with a horizontal turquoise strip across the top; front plates are not required.

notes.subject: car
notes.text: Large white pickup, usually fully blurred, with an antenna occasionally visible. The Costa Rican truck is usually unblurred.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Red octagonal signs with an oddly realistic eye are found nowhere else.

notes.subject: car
notes.text: Yellow taxis with a chequerboard stripe, and the plate drawn on the side with a city name and region code.

notes.subject: line
notes.text: Solid white edge lines with no centre line are almost unique in Latin America; white outer plus yellow inner is the commonest combination.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Stop signs read ALTO, in a thicker font than others using the word.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Mostly round concrete poles with a varying number of insulators; wooden and metal ones also occur, often with plates or painted numbers.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Hilly and tropical, with lots of palms, plus drier rolling hills and fields.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Roads are lined by fences partly or fully made of small trees, with wooden posts.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Colonial influence with bright colours and ornate detail; painted concrete or brick walls, red metal or tile roofs, barred windows.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Almost no coverage on the north coast or east of the capital.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Tall vertical yellow or white pole plates held on by black zip ties are common in the eastern provinces.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Many poles in the western provinces carry horizontal plates.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Thin yellow plates with a visible black border are most common in Colón.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Yellow pole socks appear near the Canal, around Gatún.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Lush tropical landscape with palms and very tall grass around the Caribbean port city and the capital.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Volcanic rocks, scattered or built into walls, are common north of David.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Very flat, open fields around David, with mountains visible to the north and northeast.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Fairly flat farmland with brown or orange soil around Aguadulce.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Banana plantations fill the area around Changuinola.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: The main road through Ngäbe-Buglé is very high, with dry mountains and views almost above the clouds.

notes.subject: line
notes.text: The divided concrete highway between the capital and Colón is grainy with many tar lines, through lush hills.
